title: The Last Garden Revisited
premise: Ansel Vane has spent her life mapping the Thornfell mountains and keeping her half-divine blood a secret, but when the old gods stir and prayers begin to be answered, her hidden heritage marks her as the only one who can enter the god-touched places. She discovers that King Aldric is no longer himself: something ancient wearing his crown has been feeding on his devotion, binding him to its will. Guided by a disgraced priest named Corin, whom she grows to love against every rule of duty, Ansel journeys into the unmapped heart of the mountains to unbind the king. In the climax she must surrender her invisibility—claiming her identity as the old gods' last daughter—to sever the crown's hold, and she returns not as a shadow in the margins, but as a woman who belongs, with Corin at her side.
about_author: S. M. Whitlock is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six years leading expeditions through remote mountain ranges before turning to fantasy. Their work blends cartographic precision with folklore, exploring what it costs to be seen.

chapters.title: The Margin Where Prayers Land
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. While charting a smuggler's pass, Ansel witnesses a shrine flare alive for the first time in centuries—and feels it call her by a name she buried. A dying pilgrim begs her to save King Aldric from 'the thing wearing his crown.' Ansel refuses, terrified of exposure, but the shrine's mark burns itself onto her hand. Emotional beat: dread awakening; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: A Crown That Devours
chapters.summary: Alternating Ansel and Corin's POV. Ansel infiltrates the capital as a map-seller and confirms the king's hollow-eyed devotion; Corin, a priest stripped of orders for asking too many questions, catches her spying and instead of turning her in, shows her records of vanished royal confessors. They form an uneasy alliance. Emotional beat: reluctant trust kindling between two people who have both chosen exile over belonging.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Heart
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with Corin present. Following her own unfinished maps and the burning sigil on her hand, Ansel leads Corin into the god-touched deeps where the devouring entity nests. There the truth surfaces: the entity is a forgotten god starving for worship, and only blood of the old line can unmake its binding—or inherit it. Corin offers to take her place; she realizes she loves him. Emotional beat: love declared against duty at the threshold of sacrifice.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the entity's heart—a garden grown wild inside the mountain—Ansel stops hiding and claims her name aloud, severing the crown's hold as the old gods answer her, their daughter, at last. The starving god dissolves into the garden's soil; King Aldric wakes, weeping, human again. Ansel and Corin walk out of the mountain together, mapped at last. Emotional beat: resolution through self-acceptance; invisibility traded for belonging.
